subtopics.title: The Energy Engine and Global Circulation

questions.question: The tropics have an energy surplus because:
options: They are closer to the sun than the poles
The sun's rays strike nearly vertically, concentrating energy on a small area through little atmosphere
Ocean currents deliver heat only to the equator
The ozone layer is thinner there

questions.question: The subtropical high pressure belts near 30 degrees exist because:
options: Cold polar air flows there along the surface
The oceans are coldest at that latitude
Air that rose at the equator cools aloft and subsides there
Mountains block the wind at 30 degrees

questions.question: In the southern hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects moving air to the:
options: Left
Right
East only
Equator

questions.question: The surface winds of the Hadley cell, returning from 30 degrees toward the equator, are the:
options: Westerlies
Polar easterlies
Berg winds
Trade winds

questions.question: The ITCZ is best described as:
options: A cold front circling the poles
The thundery zone where the two hemispheres' trade winds converge and rise, migrating with the overhead sun
A belt of permanent subsidence over the equator
The boundary between the Benguela and Agulhas currents

questions.question: The Kalahari High dries the Highveld winter because:
options: It pulls cold fronts over the plateau
It blows moisture out to sea
Its subsiding air suppresses cloud and rain over the interior
It freezes water vapour out of the air

questions.question: Drought differs from aridity in that drought is:
options: Rainfall significantly below what is expected for that region, while aridity is a permanent condition
Permanent dryness, while aridity is temporary
Only found in deserts
Caused by people, while aridity is natural

questions.question: Desertification is mainly driven by:
options: El Niño events alone
The natural expansion of the Sahara's sand dunes
Volcanic ash sterilising the soil
Human land misuse — overgrazing, overcultivation, deforestation and poor irrigation — which drought then exposes

subtopics.title: Reading Rock into Landscape — Horizontal, Inclined and Massive

questions.question: The erosion sequence of horizontally layered Karoo landscapes runs:
options: Conical hill, butte, mesa, plateau
Plateau, mesa, butte, conical hill
Dome, tor, mesa, plateau
Cuesta, hogsback, butte, mesa

questions.question: A butte differs from a mesa in that a butte:
options: Has no cap rock at all
Is always made of granite
Is taller than its narrow flat top is wide
Has a top wider than its height

questions.question: A cuesta's two slopes are:
options: A gentle dip slope following the tilted resistant layer, and a steep scarp slope cutting across the broken edges
Two equal steep slopes like a roof ridge
A vertical cliff on both sides
A concave slope facing north and a convex slope facing south

questions.question: Granite domes like Paarl Mountain stay rounded because:
options: They erode along their horizontal layers
Wind polishes them smooth
Glaciers rounded them in the ice age
Exfoliation peels curved shells off the pressure-released rock, which has no layers to make steps

subtopics.title: Slopes, Mass Movement and the Map

questions.question: The four slope elements from top to bottom are:
options: Pediment, talus, cliff, crest
Crest, cliff, talus, pediment
Scarp, dip, crest, plain
Cliff, crest, pediment, talus

questions.question: Leaning fence posts and curved tree trunks on a slope are evidence of:
options: Rockfall
A mudflow
Soil creep
A slump

questions.question: A slump differs from a landslide because a slump:
options: Moves along a curved surface, rotating backward and leaving a crescent scar
Only happens in solid rock
Is faster than any other movement
Moves uphill under pressure

questions.question: On a contour map, a mesa appears as:
options: Widely spaced parallel lines across the whole feature
A single spiral line
Contours forming a V pointing downstream
Crowded contours ringing a nearly empty flat top, with a widening skirt below

subtopics.title: Three Conveyor Belts and a Merry-Go-Round

questions.question: The world's great deserts sit near 30 degrees because:
options: That latitude receives the least sunlight
The air that rose and rained at the equator subsides there, dry and cloud-suppressing
Ocean currents avoid those latitudes
The ITCZ is anchored there permanently

questions.question: In the merry-go-round picture, the ball's curved path stands for:
options: The migration of the pressure belts
The rising of air at the equator
The Coriolis deflection of winds over the rotating earth
The friction between wind and ground

questions.question: Cape Town's rain arrives in winter exactly when Johannesburg's stops because:
options: The two cities share one cloud system
Cape Town's mountains only work in winter
The Agulhas current reverses in winter
The whole circulation migrates north: the ITCZ leaves the plateau dry while the westerlies' fronts reach the Cape

subtopics.title: The Layer Cake, the Tilted Books and the Rising Loaf

questions.question: In the layer cake picture, the hard chocolate top stands for:
options: The resistant dolerite cap rock protecting softer Karoo layers beneath
The soil layer above bedrock
The talus slope
A granite batholith

questions.question: The tilted books teach that as the dip of strata steepens:
options: The ridge becomes flatter on top
The dip and scarp slopes become more equal, from cuesta through homoclinal ridge to hogsback
The scarp slope becomes gentler than the dip slope
The rock stops eroding

questions.question: Tors form when:
options: Volcanoes stack cooling lava blocks
Rivers pile boulders in their beds
Water rots jointed granite at the block corners underground, and erosion removes the grit leaving rounded cores stacked
Wind carves layered sandstone into towers

questions.question: Granite landscapes never form steps or terraces because:
options: Granite is too soft to hold a step
They are protected by cap rock
Steps only form under ice sheets
Massive rock has no layers, so erosion works on one structureless body

subtopics.title: One Walk Down the Hillside — Slopes, Slides and the Exam

questions.question: On the walk, the loose angular rubble resting at the steepest angle it can hold is the:
options: Talus or scree slope
Pediment
Crest
Dip slope

questions.question: The strongest mass movement answers always name the trigger, which is nearly always:
options: Wind or lightning
Water or human interference such as undercutting and stripped vegetation
Animal burrows
Cold nights

questions.question: A cuesta announces itself on the map by:
options: Perfectly circular contour rings
Contours crossing each other on the scarp
Asymmetry — contours packed on the scarp side and widely spaced on the dip side
A single contour looping the summit

questions.question: Intervisibility between two points on a map is broken when:
options: The two points lie on the same contour
A river flows between the points
The gradient between them is gentler than 1 in 20
A convex slope or rise humps above the straight sight line between them
